title: Rigveda 7.47: To the waters
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.47: To the waters: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.47 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to the waters. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 524r-524v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.47.1-4 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 4, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 524v
translation.original_text:
1āpo̱ yaṁ va̍ḥ pratha̱maṁ de̍va̱yanta̍ indra̱pāna̍m ū̱rmim akṛ̍ṇvate̱ḻaḥ | taṁ vo̍ va̱yaṁ śuci̍m ari̱pram a̱dya ghṛ̍ta̱pruṣa̱m madhu̍mantaṁ vanema ||
2tam ū̱rmim ā̍po̱ madhu̍mattamaṁ vo̱ 'pāṁ napā̍d avatv āśu̱hemā̍ | yasmi̱nn indro̱ vasu̍bhir mā̱dayā̍te̱ tam a̍śyāma deva̱yanto̍ vo a̱dya ||
3śa̱tapa̍vitrāḥ sva̱dhayā̱ mada̍ntīr de̱vīr de̱vānā̱m api̍ yanti̱ pātha̍ḥ | tā indra̍sya̱ na mi̍nanti vra̱tāni̱ sindhu̍bhyo ha̱vyaṁ ghṛ̱tava̍j juhota ||
4yāḥ sūryo̍ ra̱śmibhi̍r āta̱tāna̱ yābhya̱ indro̱ ara̍dad gā̱tum ū̱rmim | te si̍ndhavo̱ vari̍vo dhātanā no yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
1MAY we obtain this day from you, O Waters, that wave of pure refreshment, which the pious Made erst the special beverage of Indra, bright, stainless, rich in sweets and dropping fatness.
2May the Floods' Offspring, he whose course is rapid, protect that wave most rich in sweets, O Waters, That shall make Indra and the Vasus joyful. This may we gain from you to-day, we pious.
3All-purifying, joying in their nature, to paths of Gods the Goddesses move onward. They never violate the laws of Indra. Present the oil-rich offering to the Rivers.
4Whom Sûrya with his bright beams hath attracted, and Indra dug the path for them to travel, May these Streams give us ample room and freedom. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 524v (numbered 45v by the scribe) (OPenn image 525, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.47.1 ‹-yam vaḥ prathamam dava-yantaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 525r (numbered 46r by the scribe), begins in RV 7.48.3 ‹te cit hi pūrvīḥ›. Verses 7.47.1-4 end on this page; 7.47.1 begins on fol. 524r (numbered 45r by the scribe).
